text:
maya: starting perf validation for APAC chi2 cluster (chi2-prod-1). provisioning finished but we need a short checklist: kernel/driver sanity, NIC tuning, perf baselining, and a handoff checklist. anyone can take lead?

deploybot: cluster chi2-prod-1 provisioning completed: 12 nodes (A100 80GB), 2 subnets, SGs applied. See console: https://console.redwood/chi2/chi2-prod-1 :rocket:

sylas: I can own perf runs for the next 2 hours. quick wins: kernel version, nvidia driver, and PCIe errors first.

leah: I want to run model microbenchmarks for throughput/latency comparison vs sfo baseline. will need the exact bench command.

maya: cool. start with these sanity commands on node01:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@node01
sudo dmesg | egrep -i "nvidia|nvlink|pci" | tail -n 50
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
uname -r
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || nvidia-smi -q | head
```

sylas: noted. also check for module taints and DKMS: `sudo dkms status` and `sudo modinfo nvidia | grep -i version`. Kernel/driver mismatch tends to show up in dmesg: "nvidia: probe of nvidia0 failed with error -524".

oncall-bot: Reminder: baseline job template `redwood-bench:quick-gen` available. Use --warm-cache for steady-state metrics.

leah: bench command I used locally (we should run on 1 GPU first then scale):

```bash
redwood-bench gen \
  --model redwood-7b \
  --batch 8 \
  --tokens 512 \
  --gpus 1 \
  --warm-cache \
  --report p50,p95,throughput
```

sylas: running that now on node01 (GPU0). quick results (cold start removed): p50 token latency 18ms, p95 46ms, throughput 210 tokens/s per GPU. baseline sfo-prod for same model: p95 ~40ms, throughput ~230 t/s.

maya: p95 delta looks ok-ish but we need to validate kernel micro-ops. what kernel version?

sylas: uname -r = 6.1.22-rt; nvidia driver = 535.86.05. there are a few WARNs in dmesg about missing hugepages allocations for NVLINK buffers.

leah: try increasing hugepages and set memory lock for gpu workloads. Also confirm NIC offloads: `ethtool -k eth0` and RSS/MTU. For throughput-sensitive workloads we prefer MTU 9000.

maya: commands to run for NIC tuning:

```bash
sudo ethtool -g eth0
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off || true
sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=134217728
sudo sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=134217728
# set MTU if allowed
sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000
```

sylas: did MTU -> 9000 on node01, restarted bench. throughput improved to 240 t/s, p95 down to 42ms. looks like NIC config mattered.

tj: flag: if these nodes are using preemptible/spot pools, perf jitter will be higher. for stable p95 SLAs recommend reserved capacity or dedicated nodes. cost note: reserved adds ~20% baseline cost but reduces retries and tail SLO exposures.

maya: good call. add to handoff: whether cluster is spot-backed and how to rebind workloads on spot termination.

sylas: found one kernel log line worth investigating: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31`. mild GPU ECC event on node05. open a HW ticket? we should mark node05 degraded for now.

leah: mark it in cluster inventory and exclude from autoscaler pool until validated. run `nvidia-persistenced` and run stress test: `cuda_stress --time 15m` on that node.

maya: handoff checklist draft (short):
- kernel/driver match verified (uname, nvidia-smi)
- no PCIe/NVLINK errors in dmesg (Xid lines)
- NIC tuning applied, MTU confirmed
- hugepages / memlock / sysctl tuned for perf
- bench results attached (cold vs warm, p50/p95/throughput)
- node health: exclude any nodes with ECC/Xid events
- alerts created: p95 > 2x baseline, gpu_mem_pressure > 85%, pci_errors > 0
- note whether cluster uses spot instances and recommended commit level
- ops runbook link: ops/runbooks/chi2-provisioning (create on handoff)

sylas: I'll upload raw bench logs to S3: s3://redwood-perf/chi2/1805129876/ and tag them with metadata: model, batch, tokens, warm/cold, driver, kernel.

deploybot: dashboard created: /dashboards/chi2/perf-baseline, alert `chi2-p95-regression` created with threshold = baseline_p95*1.8.

tj: assignable items: sylas (bench logs + node exclusion), leah (node05 stress + hardware ticket), maya (create runbook and link to console), tj (decide spot vs reserved and update cost forecast).

maya: thanks. final note: schedule a 30min handoff call once logs uploaded. prefer 10:30 PT. any objections?

leah: 10:30 PT works for me. :+1:

sylas: works. uploading now.

oncall-bot: Reminder set for 10:30 PT handoff meeting.
